content.text:
I made the review fixes locally: added constructor assertions, restored both uniform regression inputs, and clarified the geometry comments. Nothing has been posted or pushed.

All four geometry unit suites and three one-step mirror regressions passed. The mirror field-direction tests also passed Valgrind with no memory errors or lost allocations.

Suggested replies:

**On the formula changes and CBC `bcart`:**

> The CBC `bcart` change fixes a nodal-to-modal conversion error. The vector identity is unchanged:
> \[
> \hat{\mathbf b}=\sum_i b_i\nabla q^i.
> \]
> `gkyl_calc_metric_advance_bcart` evaluates both inputs at interior Gauss nodes and constructs `bcart` there, but previously passed `use_quad=false` when converting back to modal coefficients. That interpreted the data using the corner-node conversion. The correction uses `use_quad=true`, matching the input evaluations. This affects uniform grids too.
>
> The other geometry corrections are:
>
> - **Mirror mapping:** For \(Z=M(z)\), the field-line tangent is
>   \[
>   \mathbf e_3=M'(z)\left(-\frac{\psi_Z}{\psi_R}\hat{\mathbf R}+\hat{\mathbf Z}\right).
>   \]
>   Previously only its axial component included \(M'(z)\). The radial component needs the same chain-rule factor; otherwise the tangent is no longer tangent to constant-\(\psi\) surfaces. The updated construction also includes the radial and azimuthal map derivatives consistently in the tangents, duals, and Jacobian.
> - **Mirror field direction:** The previous expressions \(b_i=g_{i3}/\sqrt{g_{33}}\) assumed the magnetic field points along increasing third coordinate. The corrected expressions use \(\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|\), \(b_i=\mathbf e_i\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}\), and \(B^3=\nabla q^3\cdot\mathbf B\), preserving the field’s sign.
> - **Tokamak and mirror curl:** The corrected expressions follow
>   \[
>   \nabla\times(\mathbf B/B)
>   =\frac{\nabla\times\mathbf B}{B}
>   -\frac{\nabla B\times\mathbf B}{B^2}.
>   \]
>   The old expressions omitted derivatives of the cylindrical \(1/R\) factors and had incorrect signs or missing \(B^{-2}\) factors in the normalization terms. The tokamak calculation also missed a factor \(1/R\) in the toroidal contribution to \(\partial_Z B\). The mirror curl calculation previously used the opposite poloidal-field sign from the stored mirror magnetic vector; these now agree.
> - **Node placement:** Coordinates now come directly from global cell indices and the appropriate Gauss ordinates. This replaces accumulated rank-local increments and fixes the higher-order node placement.
> - **EFIT:** Where \(F=0\), computing \(F'=(FF')/F\) is undefined. Those points now use a finite difference of the tabulated \(F\).
>
> Your boundary-flux simplification in #1178 is already merged into this branch.

**On unchecked mirror constructors:**

> Agreed. I added assertions immediately after constructing the corner grid, interior grid, and each surface grid in `gk_geometry_mirror.c`. The grid generator retains its cleanup-and-NULL return behavior; the geometry caller now checks that result before using it.

**On keeping uniform tests:**

> Agreed. I removed the added `position_map_info` blocks from `rt_gk_mirror_boltz_elc_1x2v_p1` and `rt_gk_wham_1x2v_p1`, restoring their uniform computational grids. The existing WHAM `nonuniformx` tests retain the mapping coverage. Both restored inputs and the nonuniform WHAM input passed one-step smoke tests.

**On “bhat can oppose the third coordinate tangent”:**

> Here \(\mathbf e_3=\partial\mathbf X/\partial z\) points toward increasing computational \(z\). For the mirror convention,
> \[
> \mathbf B=\frac{\psi_R}{R\,M'(z)}\mathbf e_3.
> \]
> Thus they are antiparallel when \(\psi_R/M'(z)<0\). The metric determines the tangent’s length but cannot determine the magnetic-field direction. Using \(\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|\) preserves that direction. I replaced the comment with this explicit relationship.
